name: Shammua
overview: Shammua is a male descendant of Bilgah from the tribe of Levi, noted in Nehemiah 12:18. As a Levite, he is part of the priestly lineage descending from Aaron, serving in a religious capacity among God's people. His identification as a descendant of Bilgah situates him within the broader Levitical priesthood during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Shammua is a proper Hebrew name possibly meaning 'YHWH hears' or 'rumor,' reflecting a theophoric element that emphasizes God's attentiveness. This name is recorded in Nehemiah 12:18 and was not given directly by God but carries spiritual significance within the Hebrew tradition.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Shammua as a descendant of Bilgah, linking him to a specific Levitical family branch. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Shammua's significance lies in his role as a priestly descendant of Aaron, contributing to the restoration and organization of temple worship after the exile. His mention in Nehemiah 12:18 highlights the continuity of the Levitical priesthood and the faithful preservation of God's appointed religious order among the returned exiles.
